sanskrit: ye ke cana gatās tasya samīpam apalāyinaḥ na te pratinyavartanta samudrād iva sindhavaḥ
english: Whoever among the unflinching drew near to him never returned again, as rivers that have entered the sea do not flow back.

sanskrit: mahāgrāhagṛhīteva vātavegabhayārditā samakampata sā senā vibhraṣṭā naur ivārṇave
english: As though seized by a great sea-monster, tormented by terror of the wind's force, that army trembled and broke apart like a ship foundering on the ocean.

sanskrit: atha rukmaratho nāma madreśvarasuto balī trastām āśvāsayan senām atrasto vākyam abravīt
english: Then a mighty warrior named Rukmaratha, son of the lord of the Madras, himself unshaken, reassured the frightened host and spoke these words:

sanskrit: alaṃ trāsena vaḥ śūrā naiṣa kaś cin mayi sthite aham enaṃ grahīṣyāmi jīvagrāhaṃ na saṃśayaḥ
english: "Enough of your fear, O heroes! While I stand here he is nothing. I shall take him alive — of that there is no doubt."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu saubhadram abhidudrāva vīryavān sukalpitenohyamānaḥ syandanena virājatā
english: Having spoken thus, the valorous one rushed upon the son of Subhadrā, borne along by a splendid, well-fitted chariot.

sanskrit: so 'bhimanyuṃ tribhir bāṇair viddhvā vakṣasy athānadat tribhiś ca dakṣiṇe bāhau savye ca niśitais tribhiḥ
english: He pierced Abhimanyu in the chest with three arrows and roared aloud, struck him with three on the right arm and three sharp shafts on the left.

sanskrit: sa tasyeṣvasanaṃ chittvā phālguṇiḥ savyadakṣiṇau bhujau śiraś ca svakṣibhru kṣitau kṣipram apātayat
english: But the son of Phalguna, severing his bow, swiftly brought down to the earth both his arms, left and right, and his head with its fair eyes and brows.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā rukmarathaṃ rugṇaṃ putraṃ śalyasya māninam jīvagrāhaṃ jighṛkṣantaṃ saubhadreṇa yaśasvinā
english: Seeing Rukmaratha — Śalya's proud son who had sought to take him captive — broken thus by the glorious son of Subhadrā,

sanskrit: saṃgrāmadurmadā rājan rājaputrāḥ prahāriṇaḥ vayasyāḥ śalyaputrasya suvarṇavikṛtadhvajāḥ
english: those princes, O king, battle-frenzied and hard-striking, comrades of Śalya's son, their banners wrought of gold,

sanskrit: tālamātrāṇi cāpāni vikarṣanto mahārathāḥ ārjuniṃ śaravarṣeṇa samantāt paryavārayan
english: those great chariot-warriors, drawing bows tall as palm-trees, hemmed in the son of Arjuna on every side with a downpour of arrows.

sanskrit: śūraiḥ śikṣābalopetais taruṇair atyamarṣaṇaiḥ dṛṣṭvaikaṃ samare śūraṃ saubhadram aparājitam
english: Seeing that lone hero, the unconquered son of Subhadrā, amid the fray, beset by valiant youths trained in skill and full of fury,

sanskrit: chādyamānaṃ śaravrātair hṛṣṭo duryodhano 'bhavat vaivasvatasya bhavanaṃ gatam enam amanyata
english: shrouded by their swarms of arrows, Duryodhana grew glad, for he reckoned that the youth had already gone to the abode of Yama, the son of Vivasvat.

sanskrit: suvarṇapuṅkhair iṣubhir nānāliṅgais tribhis tribhiḥ adṛśyam ārjuniṃ cakrur nimeṣāt te nṛpātmajāḥ
english: With gold-feathered arrows of many marks, three by three, those king's sons in the twinkling of an eye made the son of Arjuna vanish from sight.

sanskrit: sasūtāśvadhvajaṃ tasya syandanaṃ taṃ ca māriṣa ācitaṃ samapaśyāma śvāvidhaṃ śalalair iva
english: And his chariot, O sire, with its charioteer, horses, and banner, we saw so thickly covered with shafts that it was like a porcupine bristling with quills.

sanskrit: sa gāḍhaviddhaḥ kruddhaś ca tottrair gaja ivārditaḥ gāndharvam astram āyacchad rathamāyāṃ ca yojayat
english: Deeply pierced and enraged, like an elephant goaded with hooks, he drew forth the Gāndharva weapon and called up the magic of chariot-craft.

sanskrit: arjunena tapas taptvā gandharvebhyo yad āhṛtam tumburupramukhebhyo vai tenāmohayatāhitān
english: With that weapon, which Arjuna had won through austerities from the Gandharvas led by Tumburu, he bewildered his foes.

sanskrit: ekaḥ sa śatadhā rājan dṛśyate sma sahasradhā alātacakravat saṃkhye kṣipram astrāṇi darśayan
english: That single warrior, O king, appeared a hundredfold, a thousandfold, swiftly displaying his weapons in the battle like a whirling brand of fire.

sanskrit: rathacaryāstramāyābhir mohayitvā paraṃtapaḥ bibheda śatadhā rājañ śarīrāṇi mahīkṣitām
english: Having confounded them, O king, with his chariot-evolutions and the illusions of his weapons, that scorcher of foes pierced the bodies of the lords of the earth a hundredfold.

sanskrit: prāṇāḥ prāṇabhṛtāṃ saṃkhye preṣitā niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ rājan prāpur amuṃ lokaṃ śarīrāṇy avaniṃ yayuḥ
english: The life-breaths of those creatures, sped forth in battle by his sharp arrows, O king, attained the world beyond, while their bodies went down to the earth.

sanskrit: dhanūṃṣy aśvān niyantṝṃś ca dhvajān bāhūṃś ca sāṅgadān śirāṃsi ca śitair bhallais teṣāṃ ciccheda phālguniḥ
english: Their bows, horses, drivers, banners, and arms with their armlets, and their heads as well — all these the son of Phalguna sheared off with sharp broad-headed shafts.

sanskrit: cūtārāmo yathā bhagnaḥ pañcavarṣaphalopagaḥ rājaputraśataṃ tadvat saubhadreṇāpatad dhatam
english: As a mango grove in its fifth year of fruiting is shattered, so a hundred princes fell slain by the son of Subhadrā.

sanskrit: kruddhāśīviṣasaṃkāśān sukumārān sukhocitān ekena nihatān dṛṣṭvā bhīto duryodhano 'bhavat
english: Seeing them — tender-bodied, bred to ease, yet like enraged venomous serpents — struck down by one man alone, Duryodhana was seized with fear.

sanskrit: rathinaḥ kuñjarān aśvān padātīṃś cāvamarditān dṛṣṭvā duryodhanaḥ kṣipram upāyāt tam amarṣitaḥ
english: Seeing chariot-warriors, elephants, horses, and footmen crushed alike, Duryodhana, unable to endure it, swiftly bore down upon him.

sanskrit: tayoḥ kṣaṇam ivāpūrṇaḥ saṃgrāmaḥ samapadyata athābhavat te vimukhaḥ putraḥ śaraśatārditaḥ
english: For but a moment the combat between the two ran its full course; then your son, tormented by a hundred arrows, turned his face from the fight.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca yathā vadasi me sūta ekasya bahubhiḥ saha saṃgrāmaṃ tumulaṃ ghoraṃ jayaṃ caiva mahātmanaḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: As you tell me, O charioteer, of the tumultuous, dreadful battle of that one against the many, and of the high-souled youth's victory —

sanskrit: aśraddheyam ivāścaryaṃ saubhadrasyātha vikramam kiṃ tu nātyadbhutaṃ teṣāṃ yeṣāṃ dharmo vyapāśrayaḥ
english: the prowess of the son of Subhadrā seems a marvel hard to believe; yet nothing is too wondrous for those whose refuge is righteousness.

sanskrit: duryodhane 'tha vimukhe rājaputraśate hate saubhadre pratipattiṃ kāṃ pratyapadyanta māmakāḥ
english: When Duryodhana had turned away and a hundred princes lay slain, what counsel did my men take against the son of Subhadrā?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca saṃśuṣkāsyāś calannetrāḥ prasvinnā lomaharṣiṇaḥ palāyanakṛtotsāhā nirutsāhā dviṣajjaye
english: Saṃjaya said: With mouths gone dry, eyes darting, sweating and with hair standing on end, eager only to flee, with no heart left to vanquish the foe,

sanskrit: hatān bhrātṝn pitṝn putrān suhṛtsaṃbandhibāndhavān utsṛjyotsṛjya samiyus tvarayanto hayadvipān
english: abandoning their slain brothers, fathers, sons, friends, kinsmen, and relations one after another, they fled together, urging on their horses and elephants.

sanskrit: tān prabhagnāṃs tathā dṛṣṭvā droṇo drauṇir bṛhadbalaḥ kṛpo duryodhanaḥ karṇaḥ kṛtavarmātha saubalaḥ
english: Seeing them thus routed, Droṇa, the son of Droṇa, Bṛhadbala, Kṛpa, Duryodhana, Karṇa, Kṛtavarman, and the son of Subala —

sanskrit: abhidrutāḥ susaṃkruddhāḥ saubhadram aparājitam te 'pi pautreṇa te rājan prāyaśo vimukhīkṛtāḥ
english: these too, in great wrath, charged upon the unconquered son of Subhadrā; yet they also, O king, were for the most part turned back by your grandson.

sanskrit: ekas tu sukhasaṃvṛddho bālyād darpāc ca nirbhayaḥ iṣvastravin mahātejā lakṣmaṇo ''rjunim abhyayāt
english: But one — Lakṣmaṇa, reared in ease, fearless from youth and pride, skilled in arrows, full of fierce splendor — advanced upon the son of Arjuna.

sanskrit: tam anvag evāsya pitā putragṛddhī nyavartata anu duryodhanaṃ cānye nyavartanta mahārathāḥ
english: Close behind him his father, doting on his son, turned back to the fight, and behind Duryodhana the other great chariot-warriors turned back as well.

sanskrit: taṃ te 'bhiṣiṣicur bāṇair meghā girim ivāmbubhiḥ sa ca tān pramamāthaiko viṣvag vāto yathāmbudān
english: They drenched him with arrows as clouds drench a mountain with rain; yet he alone scattered them as the wind scatters clouds in all directions.

sanskrit: pautraṃ tu tava durdharṣaṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ priyadarśanam pituḥ samīpe tiṣṭhantaṃ śūram udyatakārmukam
english: But your grandson, the unassailable Lakṣmaṇa, fair to look upon, that hero standing near his father with bow upraised,

sanskrit: atyantasukhasaṃvṛddhaṃ dhaneśvarasutopamam āsasāda raṇe kārṣṇir matto mattam iva dvipam
english: reared in utmost comfort, like a son of Kubera, lord of riches — him the son of Kṛṣṇa's sister met in battle as one rutting elephant meets another.

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇena tu saṃgamya saubhadraḥ paravīrahā śaraiḥ suniśitais tīkṣṇair bāhvor urasi cārpitaḥ
english: Closing with Lakṣmaṇa, the son of Subhadrā, slayer of hostile heroes, was struck on the arms and chest with keen, sharp-pointed arrows.

sanskrit: saṃkruddho vai mahābāhur daṇḍāhata ivoragaḥ pautras tava mahārāja tava pautram abhāṣata
english: Then the mighty-armed one, enraged like a serpent struck with a staff — your grandson, O great king — spoke to your grandson:

sanskrit: sudṛṣṭaḥ kriyatāṃ loko amuṃ lokaṃ gamiṣyasi paśyatāṃ bāndhavānāṃ tvāṃ nayāmi yamasādanam
english: "Look well upon this world, for you shall go to the next. Before the eyes of your kinsmen I send you to the abode of Yama."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tato bhallaṃ saubhadraḥ paravīrahā udbabarha mahābāhur nirmuktoragasaṃnibham
english: Having spoken thus, the mighty-armed son of Subhadrā, slayer of hostile heroes, drew forth a broad-headed shaft that gleamed like a serpent freshly sloughed of its skin.

sanskrit: sa tasya bhujanirmukto lakṣmaṇasya sudarśanam sunasaṃ subhru keśāntaṃ śiro 'hārṣīt sakuṇḍalam lakṣmaṇaṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā hā hety uccukruśur janāḥ
english: Loosed from his arm, it struck off Lakṣmaṇa's lovely head — fair-nosed, fair-browed, well-tressed, still wearing its earrings; and seeing Lakṣmaṇa slain, the people cried out, "Alas! Alas!"

sanskrit: tato duryodhanaḥ kruddhaḥ priye putre nipātite hatainam iti cukrośa kṣatriyān kṣatriyarṣabhaḥ
english: Then Duryodhana, enraged at the fall of his dear son, that bull among warriors, cried out to the kṣatriyas, "Slay him!"

sanskrit: tato droṇaḥ kṛpaḥ karṇo droṇaputro bṛhadbalaḥ kṛtavarmā ca hārdikyaḥ ṣaḍ rathāḥ paryavārayan
english: Then Droṇa, Kṛpa, Karṇa, the son of Droṇa, Bṛhadbala, and Kṛtavarman the son of Hṛdika — these six chariot-warriors closed in around him.

sanskrit: sa tān viddhvā śitair bāṇair vimukhīkṛtya cārjuniḥ vegenābhyapatat kruddhaḥ saindhavasya mahad balam
english: Piercing them with sharp arrows and turning them back, the son of Arjuna in his fury fell with speed upon the great host of the Saindhava.

sanskrit: āvavrus tasya panthānaṃ gajānīkena daṃśitāḥ kaliṅgāś ca niṣādāś ca krāthaputraś ca vīryavān tat prasaktam ivātyarthaṃ yuddham āsīd viśāṃ pate
english: The Kaliṅgas, the Niṣādas, and the valiant son of Krātha, mailed and ranged with their elephant-host, barred his path; and the fighting that followed, O lord of peoples, became unbroken and exceedingly fierce.

sanskrit: tatas tat kuñjarānīkaṃ vyadhamad dhṛṣṭam ārjuniḥ yathā vivān nityagatir jaladāñ śataśo 'mbare
english: Then the son of Arjuna scattered that elephant-host in its insolence as the ever-moving wind scatters the rain-clouds by the hundred across the sky.

sanskrit: tataḥ krāthaḥ śaravrātair ārjuniṃ samavākirat athetare saṃnivṛttāḥ punar droṇamukhā rathāḥ paramāstrāṇi dhunvānāḥ saubhadram abhidudruvuḥ
english: Then Krātha covered the son of Arjuna with showers of arrows; and the other chariot-warriors led by Droṇa, having rallied, brandishing their mightiest weapons, rushed once more upon the son of Subhadrā.

sanskrit: tān nivāryārjunir bāṇaiḥ krāthaputram athārdayat śaraugheṇāprameyeṇa tvaramāṇo jighāṃsayā
english: Warding them off with his arrows, the son of Arjuna then in his eagerness to slay tormented the son of Krātha with a measureless flood of shafts.

sanskrit: sadhanurbāṇakeyūrau bāhū samukuṭaṃ śiraḥ chatraṃ dhvajaṃ niyantāram aśvāṃś cāsya nyapātayat
english: His two arms with their bow, arrows, and armlets, his head with its diadem, his parasol, his banner, his driver, and his horses — all these he brought down.

sanskrit: kulaśīlaśrutabalaiḥ kīrtyā cāstrabalena ca yukte tasmin hate vīrāḥ prāyaśo vimukhābhavan
english: When that one — endowed with noble birth, character, learning, strength, renown, and mastery of weapons — was slain, the warriors for the most part turned away from the fight.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca tathā praviṣṭaṃ taruṇaṃ saubhadram aparājitam kulānurūpaṃ kurvāṇaṃ saṃgrāmeṣv apalāyinam
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: When the young, unconquered son of Subhadrā had thus entered in, acting worthily of his lineage, never fleeing in battle,

sanskrit: ājāneyaiḥ subalibhir yuktam aśvais trihāyanaiḥ plavamānam ivākāśe ke śūrāḥ samavārayan
english: yoked to strong, well-bred three-year-old horses, soaring as if through the sky — what heroes withstood him?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca abhimanyuḥ praviśyaiva tāvakān niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ akarod vimukhān sarvān pārthivān pāṇḍunandanaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: No sooner had Abhimanyu, the delight of the Pāṇḍus, entered in than with his sharp arrows he turned back all your kings.

sanskrit: taṃ tu droṇaḥ kṛpaḥ karṇo drauṇiś ca sabṛhadbalaḥ kṛtavarmā ca hārdikyaḥ ṣaḍ rathāḥ paryavārayan
english: But Droṇa, Kṛpa, Karṇa, the son of Droṇa together with Bṛhadbala, and Kṛtavarman the son of Hṛdika — these six chariot-warriors encircled him.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā tu saindhave bhāram atimātraṃ samāhitam sainyaṃ tava mahārāja yudhiṣṭhiram upādravat
english: But seeing the burden laid too heavily upon the Saindhava, your army, O great king, charged upon Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: saubhadram itare vīram abhyavarṣañ śarāmbubhiḥ tālamātrāṇi cāpāni vikarṣanto mahārathāḥ
english: The other great chariot-warriors, drawing bows tall as palm-trees, rained streams of arrows upon the heroic son of Subhadrā.

sanskrit: tāṃs tu sarvān maheṣvāsān sarvavidyāsu niṣṭhitān vyaṣṭambhayad raṇe bāṇaiḥ saubhadraḥ paravīrahā
english: But all those mighty archers, accomplished in every branch of knowledge, the son of Subhadrā, slayer of hostile heroes, held in check with his arrows in the field.

sanskrit: droṇaṃ pañcāśatā viddhvā viṃśatyā ca bṛhadbalam aśītyā kṛtavarmāṇaṃ kṛpaṃ ṣaṣṭyā śilīmukhaiḥ
english: He pierced Droṇa with fifty shafts, Bṛhadbala with twenty, Kṛtavarman with eighty, and Kṛpa with sixty arrows.

sanskrit: rukmapuṅkhair mahāvegair ākarṇasamacoditaiḥ avidhyad daśabhir bāṇair aśvatthāmānam ārjuniḥ
english: With ten arrows, gold-feathered and of great speed, drawn back to the ear, the son of Arjuna struck Aśvatthāman.

sanskrit: sa karṇaṃ karṇinā karṇe pītena niśitena ca phālgunir dviṣatāṃ madhye vivyādha parameṣuṇā
english: And the son of Phalguna, amid the enemy, struck Karṇa upon the ear with a sharp, yellow-tipped barbed arrow, a supreme shaft.

sanskrit: pātayitvā kṛpasyāśvāṃs tathobhau pārṣṇisārathī athainaṃ daśabhir bāṇaiḥ pratyavidhyat stanāntare
english: Having felled Kṛpa's horses and both his flanking charioteers, he struck him in return with ten arrows between the breasts.

sanskrit: tato vṛndārakaṃ vīraṃ kurūṇāṃ kīrtivardhanam putrāṇāṃ tava vīrāṇāṃ paśyatām avadhīd balī
english: Then the mighty one slew the hero Vṛndāraka, enhancer of the Kurus' fame, before the very eyes of your valiant sons.

sanskrit: taṃ drauṇiḥ pañcaviṃśatyā kṣudrakāṇāṃ samarpayat varaṃ varam amitrāṇām ārujantam abhītavat
english: The son of Droṇa let fly twenty-five small arrows at him as he, fearless, broke down the foremost of his foes one after another.

sanskrit: sa tu bāṇaiḥ śitais tūrṇaṃ pratyavidhyata māriṣa paśyatāṃ dhārtarāṣṭrāṇām aśvatthāmānam ārjuniḥ
english: But the son of Arjuna, O sire, swiftly struck Aśvatthāman in return with sharp arrows, before the eyes of the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: ṣaṣṭyā śarāṇāṃ taṃ drauṇis tigmadhāraiḥ sutejanaiḥ ugrair nākampayad viddhvā mainākam iva parvatam
english: With sixty arrows, keen-edged, well-sharpened, and fierce, the son of Droṇa pierced him, yet could not make him tremble — like Mount Maināka.

sanskrit: sa tu drauṇiṃ trisaptatyā hemapuṅkhair ajihmagaiḥ pratyavidhyan mahātejā balavān apakāriṇam
english: But he of great splendor and strength struck the son of Droṇa, his assailant, in return with seventy-three gold-feathered, straight-flying shafts.

sanskrit: tasmin droṇo bāṇaśataṃ putragṛddhī nyapātayat aśvatthāmā tathāṣṭau ca parīpsan pitaraṃ raṇe
english: Upon him Droṇa, doting on his son, let fall a hundred arrows, and Aśvatthāman eight more, seeking to shield his father in the fray.

sanskrit: karṇo dvāviṃśatiṃ bhallān kṛtavarmā caturdaśa bṛhadbalas tu pañcāśat kṛpaḥ śāradvato daśa
english: Karṇa loosed twenty-two broad-headed shafts, Kṛtavarman fourteen, Bṛhadbala fifty, and Kṛpa the son of Śaradvat ten.

sanskrit: tāṃs tu pratyavadhīt sarvān daśabhir daśabhiḥ śaraiḥ tair ardyamānaḥ saubhadraḥ sarvato niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: But the son of Subhadrā, tormented on every side by their sharp arrows, struck back at them all, ten arrows for each.

sanskrit: taṃ kosalānām adhipaḥ karṇinātāḍayad dhṛdi sa tasyāśvān dhvajaṃ cāpaṃ sūtaṃ cāpātayat kṣitau
english: The lord of the Kosalas struck him in the chest with a barbed arrow; but he brought down to the earth that king's horses, banner, bow, and charioteer.

sanskrit: atha kosalarājas tu virathaḥ khaḍgacarmadhṛt iyeṣa phālguneḥ kāyāc chiro hartuṃ sakuṇḍalam
english: Then the king of the Kosalas, deprived of his chariot, taking up sword and shield, sought to strike the earringed head from the body of the son of Phalguna.

sanskrit: sa kosalānāṃ bhartāraṃ rājaputraṃ bṛhadbalam hṛdi vivyādha bāṇena sa bhinnahṛdayo 'patat
english: But he pierced through the heart with an arrow the prince Bṛhadbala, lord of the Kosalas, and with heart cleft asunder that king fell.

sanskrit: babhañja ca sahasrāṇi daśa rājan mahātmanām sṛjatām aśivā vācaḥ khaḍgakārmukadhāriṇām
english: And he broke, O king, ten thousand great-souled warriors who bore swords and bows and hurled malign cries against him.

sanskrit: tathā bṛhadbalaṃ hatvā saubhadro vyacarad raṇe viṣṭambhayan maheṣvāsān yodhāṃs tava śarāmbubhiḥ
english: Having thus slain Bṛhadbala, the son of Subhadrā ranged through the battle, holding off your mighty archers and warriors with streams of arrows.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca sa karṇaṃ karṇinā karṇe punar vivyādha phālguniḥ śaraiḥ pañcāśatā cainam avidhyat kopayan bhṛśam
english: Saṃjaya said: Once more the son of Phalguna struck Karṇa upon the ear with a barbed arrow, and pierced him with fifty shafts, rousing him to great wrath.

sanskrit: prativivyādha rādheyas tāvadbhir atha taṃ punaḥ sa tair ācitasarvāṅgo bahv aśobhata bhārata
english: The son of Rādhā struck him back with as many again; and with his every limb thickly studded with them, he shone resplendent, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: karṇaṃ cāpy akarot kruddho rudhirotpīḍavāhinam karṇo 'pi vibabhau śūraḥ śaraiś citro 'sṛgāplutaḥ
english: In his rage he also made Karṇa stream with gushing blood; and Karṇa too, that hero, dappled with arrows and bathed in gore, shone forth.

sanskrit: tāv ubhau śaracitrāṅgau rudhireṇa samukṣitau babhūvatur mahātmānau puṣpitāv iva kiṃśukau
english: Both those high-souled warriors, their limbs spangled with arrows and drenched in blood, appeared like two kiṃśuka trees in full flower.

sanskrit: atha karṇasya sacivān ṣaṭ śūrāṃś citrayodhinaḥ sāśvasūtadhvajarathān saubhadro nijaghāna ha
english: Then the son of Subhadrā slew six valiant attendants of Karṇa, brilliant fighters, together with their horses, drivers, banners, and chariots.

sanskrit: athetarān maheṣvāsān daśabhir daśabhiḥ śaraiḥ pratyavidhyad asaṃbhrāntas tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: Then, unflustered, he struck the other mighty archers in return, ten arrows for each — and that seemed a marvel indeed.
